title: A Verifier Taxonomy and Open Benchmark for Detectability of LLM-Generated NetOps Failures
research_question: Can a machine-readable verifier taxonomy plus a public benchmark of LLM-generated network-change proposals reliably characterize which failure classes are detectably deterministic (syntax/policy/reachability/stateful) versus semantic (intent misalignment), and thereby guide deterministic verifier selection for NetOps workflows?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: A machine-readable verifier taxonomy (attributes: syntax, policy, reachability, stateful-emulation, intent-mapping) explains a nonzero fraction of variance in per-task deterministic-detectability (paired success-rate difference) across tasks (paired estimand described below).

H2: A stronger verifier class (syntax+policy+reachability/stateful) yields a higher detectability rate than a baseline lightweight syntax-only verifier by at least 0.15 (15 percentage points) on the preregistered confirmatory task set.
exploratory_questions: EQ1: Which specific injected or natural failure subclasses remain undetected by all deterministic verifier classes (taxonomy leaf-level analysis)?
EQ2: How sensitive are taxonomy-predicted detectability patterns to different hosted LLM generation prompts and seeds?
benchmark_scope: Publicly available, non-sensitive network configurations, change logs, and policy snippets (provably public GitHub repos, operator blog archives, RFC/standards examples).
Synthetic network-change tasks produced by hosted LLM API prompts (seeded) that inject controlled failure modes per injection protocol.
Taxonomy-labeled failure classes limited to: syntax, policy-violation, reachability-break, stateful-emulation-failure, ambiguous-intent / semantic-mismatch.
model_scope: Hosted LLM API(s) (single hosted_llm_api family for generation and for automated intent-mapper adjudication). Exact model identifiers will be recorded in the execution manifest at runtime (hosted_model_api_available per capability manifest).
transformation_scope: Provenance-based corpus filtering and deterministic anonymization (regex-based IP/AS removal and canonicalization).
Deterministic failure injection scripts (seeded) to create engineered misconfigurations and ambiguity templates.
Taxonomy attribute mapping transforms that produce machine-readable verifier capability descriptors.
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (per paired_binary_analysis_v1 contract): the mean within-task difference in binary detection (1=detected by verifier-class, 0=not detected) where each task is evaluated under baseline verifier (syntax-only exemplar) and guarded verifier (syntax+policy+reachability/stateful exemplar).
secondary_estimands: per-verifier-class detection coverage (proportion detected) across confirmatory tasks (descriptive).
sensitivity analysis estimand: paired difference under failed_call_treatment=complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity.
sampling_plan: Paired within-task design. Each task = single network-change proposal (either natural from public corpus or LLM-generated proposal with injected failure). For each task we run: (a) baseline verifier exemplar (syntax-only Docker oracle) and (b) guarded verifier exemplar (syntax+policy+reachability/stateful Docker oracle). Outcome per task is binary: detected/not-detected by each verifier class. Confirmatory sample = N paired tasks as specified in budget scenarios. Inclusion: only items with provable public provenance metadata or generated by the seeded injection scripts will be included. Exclusion: items failing deterministic provenance checks or anonymization steps are automatically excluded (deterministic flagging). Randomization: task selection for confirmatory set is randomized by a fixed RNG seed; injection variants assigned deterministically by seed schedule. All counts below explicitly show derivation (methods × tasks/per-method = totals).
analysis_plan: Primary analysis uses the registered executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 computing paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline with two-sided alpha=0.05. Primary treatment of failed calls: 'complete_pair_primary' (complete-pair analysis excluding technical infrastructure failures flagged deterministically); sensitivity analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity'. We will preregister exact mapping from verifier outputs to binary detection (detected if oracle returns a non-empty deterministic violation trace as defined in oracle spec). The analysis executor will also produce per-task confusion matrices and clustered detectability heatmaps. All analysis inputs (per-task pair binary outcomes, seeds, verifier logs) are stored and hashed in the execution manifest for reproducibility.
multiplicity_plan: One preregistered primary confirmatory hypothesis (H2 above). Secondary and exploratory analyses (per-verifier-class, leaf-level failure subclass analyses) are exploratory and will report unadjusted p-values but include multiplicity-controlled summaries using Benjamini–Hochberg where appropriate; exploratory findings are explicitly labeled as exploratory.
missingness_plan: Technical failures (e.g., runtime container crash, API outage) are detected deterministically by execution harness and logged. Primary analysis uses complete_pair_primary: any pair with an infrastructure/technical failure is excluded and reported in a technical-failure log. Sensitivity analysis treats technical failure as detection=0 per 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity'. No human adjudication is permitted; ambiguous verifier outputs are mapped to detection=0 by deterministic rule if they do not contain a canonical violation token defined in each oracle spec.

risk_factors: inclusion of vendor-sensitive or private config snippets in corpus
LLM generation copying verbatim from non-public sources (data contamination)
label leakage between confirmatory and exploratory splits
detection_procedures: Provenance-check engine: require source URL domain whitelist; reject items without traceable public origin.
Deterministic pattern scanner (regex/hard rules) to flag private-identifying tokens (emails, private ASNs, internal hostnames); flagged items are excluded automatically.

LLM-output similarity check against included public-corpus artifacts using exact-substring hashing; any near-exact matches to external non-public identifiers (none expected) will trigger automatic exclusion.
item_flagging_rules: Exclude any corpus item lacking a documented public source URL.
Exclude items with non-empty matches to private-identifier regex set (automated).
For LLM-generated proposals, only include outputs from seeded prompts; if similarity hash to excluded item > 0.9, drop and re-seed automatically (deterministic re-seeding policy).
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Flagged/excluded items are removed before sampling. All exclusions and re-seed events are logged; sensitivity analyses will report results with and without re-seeded LLM outputs.
residual_uncertainty: Some public artifacts may themselves originate from sanitized versions of private configs; representativeness is not guaranteed.
LLM training-data provenance cannot be fully ascertained; residual contamination risk remains and is documented as noncritical.

budget_scenarios.description: Lower-cost feasibility run for limited confirmatory power: paired confirmatory tasks = 50; exploratory tasks = 25; total task clusters = 75.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Estimate 10 hosted LLM calls per task (generation + intent-mapper + auxiliary prompts) → 75 × 10 = 750 planned_model_calls. Docker verifier runs and CPU emulation executed on CPU host; within capability manifest limits (maximum_planned_model_calls=10000).

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended confirmatory run balancing power and cost: paired confirmatory tasks = 100; exploratory tasks = 50; total task clusters = 150 (recommended).
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 10 hosted LLM calls per task × 150 tasks = 1500 model calls. This fits the capability manifest (<=10000 calls, CPU execution for oracles via Docker). Power analysis (see power_plan) supports 100 paired tasks to detect a 15 percentage-point improvement with >80% power under conservative variance assumptions.

budget_scenarios.description: Ambitious run for finer subgroup analysis: paired confirmatory tasks = 200; exploratory tasks = 100; total task clusters = 300.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: 10 hosted LLM calls per task × 300 tasks = 3000 planned_model_calls. Still under maximum_planned_model_calls=10000; CPU-executed Docker oracles remain the verifier execution path.

power_plan.target_effect: 0.15 (15 percentage points improvement in detection rate for guarded vs baseline)
power_plan.clustering_unit: single network-change task (paired evaluation baseline vs guarded per task)
power_plan.calculation_method: Normal-approximation paired-proportion sample-size: conservative variance p*(1-p) with p=0.5 upper bound; two-sided alpha=0.05, power=0.8 -> required N ≈ 88 pairs; preregister rounding to 100 pairs for recommended scenario.
assumptions: Within-task outcomes are paired and independent across tasks.
Conservative variance assumption p(1-p)=0.25 used for sample-size; effect size delta=0.15 is the minimally interesting detectability improvement.
Primary analysis uses paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor; failed_call_treatment primary = complete_pair_primary; sensitivity = complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity.
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With N=100 pairs, two-sided alpha=0.05, power≈0.80 can detect delta≈0.15 under conservative variance. If observed baseline detection ≪0.5, power improves; we will report achieved power post-hoc given observed baseline.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute paired difference treating technical failures as detection=0 (failed_call_treatment sensitivity).
Subset analyses stratified by failure-class (syntax vs semantic) to show heterogeneity; these are exploratory and multiplicity-adjusted where reported.

semantic_equivalence_checks: After anonymization, each corpus item is validated by deterministic parse tests ensuring syntactic structure preserved (e.g., CLI parse, JSON lint); mismatched parses cause automatic rejection.
Injected-failure templates include canonical markers; injected and post-processed artifacts are checked via exact-hash pairs to guarantee intended mutation applied deterministically.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject corpus item if provenance URL missing or not in domain whitelist (automated).
Reject item if anonymization removes >30% of tokens in a way that breaks syntactic parsability (automated).
Reject LLM-generated proposal if similarity hash to any excluded item >0.9; in that case apply deterministic re-seed and record event.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Deterministic unit tests (CI-style) exercised on a fixed small archive (10 items) packaged in the Docker artifact; these unit tests run automatically and must pass for artifact release. No human audit is required.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Taxonomy attributes are machine-readable JSON fields; mapping rules include example-driven unit tests (input→expected attribute vector). Mapping validation uses deterministic string/AST pattern matches and sample-based rule coverage checks.
residual_risks: Automated mapping may misclassify subtle hybrid verifier behaviors; this is a documented noncritical uncertainty mitigated by clear attribute definitions.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Public-corpus representativeness: available public artifacts may not span all vendor/production idiosyncrasies (external-validity limitation).
Taxonomy granularity: hybrid verifier implementations may exhibit mixed capabilities not perfectly captured by finite axes; this may reduce predictive power at leaf level.
LLM training-data provenance: inability to fully rule out private-data leakage into hosted LLMs remains a residual contamination risk documented in contamination_plan.
Community adoption: packaging and documentation may still affect ease of external reproduction despite containerized oracles.
